captions.text: In a cryptarithm, a letter stands for one digit
wherever it appears.
Different letters use different digits when the
question says so.
Work by place value.
A carry is an extra clue linking one column to the
next.
An AMC number puzzle may replace digits with letters or
boxes.
Check whether repeated symbols are required to have the
same value.
In a Rossmoyne style puzzle, a leading digit or the
size of the answer can cut down the possible carries
first.
The same digit A is added to itself and the result is
eight.
Which digit is A?
Keep both copies of A the same while you solve the
number sentence.
The left side is twice the digit A.
Dividing the whole result by two keeps the equality
balanced.
Half of eight is four.
Substitute the digit in both places to check the
original addition.
A and B are distinct digits with sum eight.
Adding thirty-six to the two-digit number A B reverses
its digits.
Both numbers have two digits.
Which digits fit the sum and the reversal together?
A B means ten A plus B.
B A means ten B plus A.
Subtract them.
The difference is nine times B minus A, with the digit
difference taken first.
The difference in the two digits is four, because
thirty-six divided by nine is four.
Subtract that from the given sum and split the
remainder in half.
A is two and B is six.
Check the two-digit numbers in the original order.
A B plus A C gives B D zero.
A, B, C and D are four distinct digits and A and B are
nonzero.
Find the smallest possible two-digit number A B.
Start with the fact that a carry creates the hundreds
digit.
Adding two two-digit numbers can carry just one
hundred.
Therefore B is one.
The units add to a number ending in zero.
One plus C can only make ten, so C is nine and one ten
carries.
The tens then give twice A plus one.
It must reach ten, and the units of that calculation
give D.
Try A equals five.
It makes D one, already used by B.
Six works.
The tens rule and distinct digits rule give the first
allowable choice in the required order.
The required number is sixty-one.
Add sixty-one and sixty-nine to verify the result one
hundred and thirty.
Treat A B as a two-digit number.
A is worth ten times as much in the tens place as it
would be in the units.
Look for a leading zero and a repeated value assigned
to different letters.
Check every symbol after the arithmetic works.
Write the columns and mark the possible carries.
Use the very first digit of a three-digit sum to narrow
your options.
After solving, put each value back into the original
expression.
An equality and a legal assignment are both required.
